findings.title: Generator rules cut reductions from 29% of FRESH-2 to 5.7% of FRESH-3; the one cell where the control led earlier nearly vanishes
findings.problem: FRESH-3 is 283 list / 8 int / 9 bool. Two generator rules cause this, not the new pairs. (i) Stage instances are de-duplicated, so the candidate list is already 78/7/13: only 5 int and 9 bool distinct second stages stand behind FRESH-2's 11 and 18 tasks. (ii) The 'public outputs all equal' test, with a uniform draw of inputs, keeps 28% of int and 13% of bool candidates against 78% of list candidates; 28 of the 45 rejected bool candidates are not constant functions, the draw just showed one value. In the earlier result every control-only solve was a reduction, and the control led on reductions without a modulo-type routine (7 sound against 4). On list outputs the trained state led 24 to 17 with no control-only solve. S and R act on list outputs only (hybrid.py lines 524 and 555-556), so reductions are solved by direct search alone, where a larger budget counts most. The mix therefore tilts the primary comparison and Q7 toward the trained arm. A positive result could say nothing about reductions (17 tasks), although the claim says 'held-out composition tasks'. The draft's explanation ('the equal-public-outputs test rejects mostly reductions') covers only part of the cause.

findings.title: The lead being replicated sits in one routine family, and neither registered test can tell one symbol family from a general effect
findings.problem: In the earlier result the whole lead is in FRESH-2 tasks with a modulo-type routine in a stage: 20 against 13 sound there, 14 against 14 in the other 70. That matches the one filter symbol the README names. FRESH-3 reuses those stage instances: 95 of 300 tasks contain a modulo-type routine. The deciding sign test counts 300 tasks as independent, but they are re-pairings of 26 first-stage and 31 second-stage routines, and 8 second-stage routines hold 184 tasks. A learned symbol acts on a routine, so discordant tasks will come in blocks. The cluster test is only 'reported without deciding anything'. It also clusters by routine name, which splits the modulo family into 4 first-stage and 6 second-stage clusters, so one symbol family alone could give p = 0.016 there. A positive outcome could be 'the modulo symbol again on re-pairings of the same stages' and still be classed 'replicated' and read as 'the learned vocabulary helps on new compositions'.

findings.title: 50 tasks are parameter variants of FRESH-2 tasks, and the text claims new parameters that do not exist
findings.problem: Candidates exclude only exact FRESH-2 pairs (routine and parameters). A pair that repeats a FRESH-2 task's two routines with a parameter taken from another task is kept: 50 of 300 tasks, 21 of which share one whole stage instance with that FRESH-2 task. These are the nearest things to the 124 tasks the combination was chosen on, so their outcomes are not independent of the selected result. Every stage instance is copied with its parameters from FRESH-1 or FRESH-2, so there is no new parameter value: 'it tests new pairs and parameters' is wrong. 'New pairs of the routines the loop trained on' also understates the overlap: in 135 tasks both stages are themselves learning tasks, routine and parameter. That share is the same as in FRESH-2, so it is a matter of wording, not of bias.

findings.title: A null would be read as 'specific to the tasks it was chosen on', but FRESH-3 also differs from FRESH-2 in its inputs
findings.problem: Inputs are drawn uniformly from the set of distinct public input lists, which drops the multiplicity of common inputs. The empty list is a public input in 1 of 300 FRESH-3 tasks against 52 of 100 FRESH-2 tasks. The longest public input has median length 10 against 7. 50 of 300 tasks hold a negative value against 4 of 100. I see no arm this favours. But a null result is confounded with the input change (and with the mix of finding 1), so the registered reading over-attributes it. Also, the audit keeps lengths between the shortest and longest example, so on FRESH-3 it almost never tests the empty list: 'sound' is a weaker statement there than on held-out B, in both arms.

coverage:
No solver was run on FRESH-3; I ran only the generator, reference functions, the audit-input generator and a stub harness. Scripts and their outputs are in <scratch>/work/confounds (a_basics.py, b_independence.py, c_whatif.py, d_last.py, e_final.py, f_table.py; b_out.txt, c_out.txt, d_out.txt).

What held:
- Generator: tallies, the 283/8/9 mix, digest 333e350613873b88 and determinism reproduce. My re-implementation gives the same fates for the 469 examined candidates.
- Reference functions: for all 300 tasks the name, the stages and all 16 examples agree with stage 2 applied after stage 1 under the selected readings (0 disagreements). I checked 18 tasks by hand, including the multi-reading routines: rotate-k is a right rotation (pinned by 11 FRESH tasks), slice-k-n is start k with length n (8 tasks), dup doubles each element, dedup is adjacent.
- Readings: all 39 routines of FRESH-1/2 have exactly one reading that fits every task, so none is left out. All 338 exposed tasks have a validated reference.
- Domain handling: inputs where stage 1 is undefined, non-list or beyond the caps are never used, and the audit skips None. The DSL's mod is Python's %, so references on the few negative values (17 of 866 pool inputs) are expressible with the same primitive.
- Independence from exposed tasks: no FRESH-3 task equals an exposed reference on all its usable pool inputs (3 at >= 0.9 agreement, 28 at >= 0.75). The first-reading shortcut of the same-function test misses nothing (0).
- No-op stages and single routines: 3 tasks have a no-op stage on all 16 examples. 10 tasks equal one routine with some parameter, 8 of them from trained families. These would favour the trained arm but are 3% of the set.
- Under-determined tasks: 8 tasks have public examples that fit a simpler function the hidden examples refute. They are lost for both arms.
- Twin test: no pair of FRESH-3 tasks agrees on >= 90% of common inputs.
- Overlap with learning tasks: the share of stages that are themselves learning tasks equals FRESH-2's (84% and 53%). FRESH-3 has the same share of modulo-type tasks as FRESH-2 (32% against 30%).
- Other generator rules: the identity test rejected 0 candidates, the caps 20 (too few inputs), the twin test 8. I found no arm these favour.
- Leakage in code: by reading and by a stub trace (d_last.py), expert.run names only the 8 exposed partitions for student runs and the 6 learning partitions for teacher runs, and reads public tasks of learning partitions only. 'fresh3' is never named or read. family_of and the corpus come from learning partitions; the gate uses the learning score. The input pool uses public inputs only. Workers receive FRESH-3 public views only in the evaluation step. Optional hardening: call harness.add_partition('fresh3', ...) after expert.run returns.
- Hidden examples, 8 against 1 or 2: no consequence for the sound comparison between arms. A wrong first match is lost either way (rejected on FRESH-3, verified but unsound on FRESH-2). It only moves verified counts toward sound counts, so verified counts are not comparable across the two sets.
- Audit: every FRESH-3 task gets 200 audit inputs. 3 tasks have audit outputs beyond the generator's caps, which the evaluator allows (4096-bit integers).
- Quotas: 213/33/54 by output type are feasible from the existing candidate list.

Not checked: budget accounting (T, C1, C2), engine and worker determinism, compress.py, and the statistics code beyond the lines cited.

findings.title: A wrong first match ends the control's run before its budget is spent, and the draft reads those tasks as wins over 'the entire budget'
findings.problem: hybrid.solve returns the first program that fits the public examples and stops. If that program is wrong (rejected by the verifier, or verified and unsound) the task is lost and the rest of the budget is never used: on those tasks C2 is a ceiling, not a cost. On held-out B this happens to generation 0 at 251,479 on 22 of 124 tasks (9 rejected, 13 verified-unsound; 18 stop inside 10^5 candidates). For 11 of the 22 it is the same program already returned at 10^4, so no budget and no union over budgets changes it. In the one positive result (44 v 37 against 569,881), 5 of the 11 trained-only tasks are of this kind: the control had stopped at 4%, 9%, 11%, 33% and 50% of its budget. Only 6 are tasks on which it spent the budget and found nothing. Addendum 7 names verifier-rejected matches only (the verified-unsound group is the larger one), licenses 'solves more than the same machinery without it does with the entire budget' from all discordant tasks alike, and replicate.py computes no split and keeps neither the stop point of a rejected match nor the candidates a run actually used. A positive primary outcome would mix two effects (programs out of reach of 7 times the budget; a different program found first), and a sceptic can reject the equal-cost reading for the second.

Sign test, all discordant 11 v 4: p = 0.059; budget-bound tasks alone, 6 v 0 to 6 v 2: p = 0.016 to 0.145. Text: PREDICTIONS.md lines 283-285, 349-350, 372-374. Code: replicate.py lines 168-173 ('rejected' holds names only; no per-task candidates).
findings.proposed_change: (1) PREDICTIONS.md, Outcome measure, replace the last sentence by: 'A run stops at its first public match. If that program is wrong (rejected by the verifier, or verified and not sound) the task is lost for that run in both arms and the rest of the budget is not spent: a budget is a ceiling. Each task only one arm solves is classed by the other arm's run on it: budget-bound (no public match within its budget) or first-match (a wrong program, with the candidates at which it stopped).' (2) Primary outcome: keep the test and add: 'The words "with the entire budget" are claimed only if the trained state also leads on the budget-bound tasks alone (more trained-only than control-only). If the test passes and it does not, the outcome is "replicated as a first-match effect": the vocabulary changes which program is found first; it is not shown to beat budget.' In the claim line write 'under a budget ceiling equal to the whole training and deployment budget'. (3) replicate.py measure(): add "stops": {f"{p}/{r['name']}": [r["route"], r["to_solution"]] for every record with r["term"] is not None} and "spent": the sum of r["candidates"]. After the audit, for trained@deploy v gen0@C2:fresh3 (and v C1 and C2 on held-out B), count the four cells (trained-only / control-only by budget-bound / first-match: a discordant key is first-match when it is in the losing row's "stops"), print them, and apply rule (2) in outcome_class. Optional: the same "spent" sum in expert.measure, so T is shown as spend beside its ceiling.

findings.title: 'Any budget' on FRESH-3 is three budgets with nothing between 10^5 and C2, where one of the two measured budget losses sits
findings.problem: The control is not monotone in budget: the shares of S and R grow with the budget, so a larger run can return a different, wrong first match. The union is the right repair for that, and replicate.py computes it as registered. It only sees the budgets that are run. On held-out B the union over the five recorded budgets is 39 sound; over the three that correspond to FRESH-3's grid (10^4, 10^5, top) it is 38; the top run alone has 37. One task is sound only at 181,775 and unsound at 251,479 and 569,881. FRESH-3's grid is 10^4, 10^5 and about 700,000, so the row 'Replicated strongly ... against "any budget"' promises more than is run. The union also does nothing for the larger group in finding 1 (the same wrong program at every budget).

findings.problem: T + D is engine candidates at their ceilings. Three things the trained arm uses are in no budget: compression in the driver (compress.propose, up to 60 calls per attempt), the verifier's verdicts on the hidden examples of the 214 learning tasks in every run (the gate and the harvest read them; 16 runs x 214 = 3,424 verdicts in the recorded loop), and the reference re-checks. In candidates the accounting errs in the control's favour (see coverage), so this is a wording gap, not a miscount.

coverage:
All work is in <scratch>/work/control-fairness (scripts a1 to a10, b1_trace.py with an instrumented copy hybrid.py, lift/b2_lift.py). Solver runs: generation 0 on the exposed partitions only, 2000 candidates, 2 workers. FRESH-3: generator only, plus element_table / filter_table on its public examples (no engine, no harness).

Checked and held:
- Early stops: none. Every task with no public match spent exactly its budget (176 of 176 at 10^4, 122 of 122 at 251,479). The registered engine at 10^6 ends all 153 unsolved tasks at size level 8 (max_size 20), none exhausted. In the 2000-candidate trace no sub-search or direct search was ended by the stop rule or PATIENCE, and failed sub-searches spent 1.000 of their share.
- Route split (hybrid.py lines 544, 557, 569, 592): S half, R scan a tenth, each of at most two pre-images a third of what is left, direct the rest. Worst case for the direct route is 13% (S fails and two pre-images fail) or 30% (two pre-images fail). Measured at 2000 on held-out B: 74 of 80 unsolved list tasks kept 88.8% for the direct route, 4 kept 38.8%, 1 kept 59.2%, 1 kept 29.8%. The R scan is repeated by the direct route (3,773 of 3,773 kept programs rebuilt on the 49 tasks with no abduced constant), so a tenth is spent twice in both arms. At 251,479 the 13 list tasks solved by the direct route had spent 10.4% to 10.8% before it; all 17 R-route solves came from the first pre-image candidate.
- The split costs the control nothing against a plain search of equal budget on exposed tasks: all 155 sound solves of the registered engine within 251,479 (338 tasks) are sound solves of the control at 251,479; on held-out B, 20 of 20 at 569,881.
- Accounting: T by replicate.py's formula equals the sum of the ceilings of the 16 recorded runs (180,220,000). It is conservative for the control: the loop used at most 38.0% of T, 11.9% of T is teacher_final and 6.2% is student runs on held-out tasks no decision reads, while the control at 251,479 used 59.6% of its ceiling. With that T, C2 = 700,733 and C1 = 621,953 on FRESH-3. Nothing is charged to the control that should not be.
- Same machinery: both arms go through spec_of with components SCfR and the restored vocabulary; ADMITTED and VECTOR are cleared per spec and CONST_WITNESS cannot change a result; compress.py admits ground parameter types only, which spec_without's TYPES covers.
- The draft's numbers reproduce from the files: 44 v 37, 11 v 4 (p = 0.059), union 39, 9 v 4 (p = 0.13).
- C2 on FRESH-3: acceptable as equal total cost in candidate ceilings, and the primary should keep it, read with the split of finding 1.

Not checked: any solver on FRESH-3; anything above 2000 candidates. How many pre-image candidates a 70,000-candidate scan finds is unknown: with the limit lifted, a 2000-candidate scan gives two or more on 14 of 90 held-out B list tasks and more than two on 5, and the share can only grow. FRESH-3 has 247 of 300 tasks on that path (36 start with S, 17 are scalar), against 80 of 124 on held-out B. Memory and time of the 1.55M-candidate C2 run on held-out B, the largest budget this harness has run, were not tested; it runs before the primary control.

findings.title: The pilot lead is one routine family (divisibility); FRESH-3 holds more of it, and neither the table nor the cluster tests can show that
findings.problem: The 11 against 4 behind the claim lies entirely in the FRESH-2 tasks that contain a routine whose name contains `mod`: 8 against 0 on those 22 tasks, 3 against 4 on the other 78 (trained 16 sound, control 17). The draft never says so. FRESH-3 has 94 such tasks of 300 (31% against 22%). If that family effect carries over and nothing changes elsewhere, the primary passes almost surely, the table says "Replicated", and the licence sentence speaks of "new pairs of the routines" in general while the trained state is behind outside the family. The registered cluster tests would not flag it: the family is 4 first-stage and 5 second-stage routines and its 94 tasks touch 25 of the 26 first-stage clusters and 20 of the 31 second-stage clusters.

findings.title: The primary control is a single run at C2, and generation 0 loses tasks when its budget grows; "Replicated" can rest on tasks it solves with less

Generation 0 at C2 is therefore not generation 0's best use of that budget. In the pilot 2 of the 11 trained-only tasks are sound for generation 0 at a smaller budget; at 569,881 it verified a different, wrong program first. Those two tasks are the whole distance between p = 0.059 and p = 0.133. The table asks for "any budget" only for "Replicated strongly", so "Replicated" can be declared, and the sentence "more than the same machinery ... does with the entire budget" quoted, when generation 0 across the budgets it was run at is not behind.

findings.title: "With the entire budget" over-reads: on 5 of the 11 pilot wins generation 0 had stopped at a wrong program long before its budget ran out
findings.problem: A run ends at its first public match. Where that match is wrong the task is lost at any budget, so the comparison on that task is not vocabulary against budget. findings.title: The cluster-level sign tests answer neither question they are registered for, and no reading is fixed for when they disagree with the task-level test
findings.problem: The stated reason is validity ("tasks that share a routine are not independent"). Validity is not at risk: the 300 tasks are a seeded random draw from the 4,385 candidate pairs, so the exact sign test is valid, and slightly conservative, for that population of pairs whatever routines they share, for this one vocabulary and this control. What shared routines limit is breadth, and there the two tests fail: each ignores the other stage, so a lead carried by a single second-stage routine gives a significant first-stage cluster test; a family that spans routines passes both; and the draft does not say which of the two p-values counts or what is written when the task level passes and a cluster level does not. As a gate they would also be costly: for a broad effect of the pilot's size, requiring both lowers the pass rate from 0.87 to 0.63. On the pilot itself they give 8 against 4 (p = 0.19) and 8 against 2 (p = 0.055).
findings.evidence: <scratch>/work/statistics/power.py, on the real FRESH-3 routine layout: effect in one second-stage routine only (identify-is-mod-k, 21 tasks): "'primary': 0.926, 'cluster first-stage p<0.05': 0.909, 'cluster second-stage p<0.05': 0.0". Broad effect (every task 11/124 and 4/124): "'primary': 0.869, 'cluster first-stage p<0.05': 0.735, 'cluster second-stage p<0.05': 0.731, 'primary and both cluster tests': 0.634". Family-only effect: both cluster tests pass in 0.744. pilot.py: "clusters by first-stage routine: for trained 8, for control 4, p=0.1938"; "by second-stage routine: for trained 8, for control 2, p=0.0547". fresh3.py printed "candidates": 4385, "examined": 469, "made": 300. The `clustered` function itself computes what it documents (checked on a hand case).
findings.proposed_change: Do not make a cluster test part of the primary rule; let Family M and leave-one-routine-out (first finding) carry breadth. Replace "because tasks that share a routine are not independent" with: "The 300 tasks are a seeded random draw from the 4,385 candidate pairs, so the task-level test is valid for that population of pairs for this vocabulary. Shared routines limit breadth, not validity. Of the two cluster-level p-values the larger is the one quoted. If the task-level test passes and that value is >= 0.05 the report says: 'The lead holds over pairs (W against L, p = ...). Over routines it does not (p = ... by first stage, ... by second stage): it is carried by <the routines with a positive net, with their nets>. Nothing is claimed for routines outside that list.'" Add: "p-values on held-out B and pooled are descriptive: held-out B is not a sample and is the set the combination was chosen on."

findings.title: Outcomes the table does not cover, and one row whose reading the design cannot support
findings.problem: (1) Row 2 reads a failure on FRESH-3 as "the earlier lead is specific to the tasks it was chosen on". The run changes two things at once: the tasks, and the mechanism (R inside the loop, hence another vocabulary). If the new state has no lead on held-out B either, the loop did not rebuild the combined state and nothing follows about the earlier lead. (2) No class is defined when a run is missing, the set is not the registered one, or the loop was restarted: replicate.py prints the FRESH-3 digest but never compares it with the registered 333e350613873b88 or checks that 300 tasks were made. (3) Sound decides the class; nothing says what is written if the same rule on verified counts gives another class. (4) "A lead over C1 on held-out B" can hold while the trained state is behind C2 on held-out B (Q5 predicts that comparison, the table ignores it). (5) The disclosure that generation 0 was run at up to 9,948 candidates per task on the first 100 tasks sits beside "no decision ... has read an outcome on it at a real budget"; 9,948 is the registered student budget of 10^4 to within 0.5%, and no analysis on the 200 untouched tasks is registered.

coverage:
Read: Addendum 7 and Addenda 3 to 6 of PREDICTIONS.md; README sections on counting, the combination, predictions, verdict, review, limits; replicate.py, fresh3.py, expert.py, audit_all.py, oracles.py, hybrid.solve and Harness, rsi5/verifier.py, rsi5/partitions.py. Ran the generator, the audit's input maker and the audit on recorded pilot programs only; no solver on anything, nothing on FRESH-3 beyond its generator and references. Scripts and outputs are in <scratch>/work/statistics (pilot.py, pilot2.py, pilot3.py, structure.py, power.py, checks3.py).

Answers that held.
- Arithmetic: 11 against 4 is 1941/32768 = 0.0592; 9 against 4 is 1093/8192 = 0.1334. Recomputed from the recorded files with the audit: 44 sound against 37, 11 and 4 discordant, union over five budgets 39, 9 and 4. All 15 discordant tasks are FRESH-2; COMPOSE-24 contributes none.
- sign_test, paired and clustered do what they document; rounding p to 5 places never changes p < 0.05 for any split up to 300 discordant tasks; outcome_class applies the table's rows in order; "final student" is the last accepted state; "any budget" unions the budgets the text lists.
- Power of the primary rule on 300 tasks (20,000 simulated draws): 0.87 at the pilot's rates per task (11/124 and 4/124), 0.93 at the FRESH-2 rates (11/100, 4/100), 0.65 at the any-budget rates (9/124, 4/124), 0.60 if the true odds are 2:1, 0.27 at 1.5:1. With no effect it passes 0.035 to 0.040. Smallest passing splits: 5-0, 7-1, 9-2, 10-3, 12-4, 13-5. The pilot estimate was selected after the fact, so the first figures are upper readings.
- The test is the right one for the stated population: an exact one-sided McNemar test on a seeded random sample of pairs, valid without any independence assumption between tasks. Its limits are scope (one vocabulary, one generator's task mix), covered in the findings.
- Sound verdict, symmetry between arms: audit inputs depend on the task key only; the audit, the verifier and the engine share the step budget of 2000; printing and re-parsing a program is faithful (0 of 55 trained and 0 of 50 control pilot programs fail an example of their own task afterwards); unsound verdicts are wrong values in 23 of 24 cases (one evaluation error, on the control side); replacing the 200 chosen inputs by the whole in-range pool (about 3,000) changes no verdict on the 85 FRESH-2 pilot programs (34 and 27 sound both ways). I found no route by which the verdict treats the arms differently.
- Sound on FRESH-3 against FRESH-2: same input maker; every FRESH-3 task gets 200 inputs; value span median 16 in both, longest input median 10.5 against 7. Differences: one reading (the generating function) against any validated reading; 8 hidden examples against 1 or 2, so on FRESH-3 verified and sound will nearly coincide and wrong first matches will show as rejections. Sound is comparable across the two sets; verified is not.
- The generator reproduces digest 333e350613873b88 and is deterministic; tally 4,385 candidates, 469 examined, 300 made; 283 list, 8 integer, 9 boolean.

Not checked: budget accounting of T, C1 and C2, the generator's filters, leakage paths, the loop itself, and anything that needs a solver run.

findings.title: The largest control run needs about three times the memory of anything run so far, and a crash there comes after FRESH-3 rows are printed
findings.problem: gen0@C2:heldB will run at about 1.5 to 1.66 x 10^6 candidates per task; the largest hybrid run so far was 569,881. The engine keeps every behaviourally distinct program, with its output vector and key, until the task ends. The pool is an executor that never replaces a worker, so one worker killed for memory ends replicate.py. That row is sixth of seven. Four FRESH-3 rows have already been printed and saved by then, and evaluation rows cannot be resumed: --from-loop reruns all seven. If the crash repeats, a person has to change something after seeing partial FRESH-3 output. I could not see the machine's RAM, so this is a risk, not a measured failure.
findings.evidence: work/implementation/state_dep.py (tracemalloc inside a worker, 10 held-out B tasks unsolved by generation 0) printed: 'budget 500: ... bytes per candidate 1579', 'budget 1000: ... 1511', 'budget 2000: ... 1827'. Linear extrapolation: 2.3 to 3.0 GB per worker at 1.5 to 1.66 x 10^6, against 0.9 to 1.0 GB at 569,881; replicate.py defaults to 4 workers. The extrapolation is over a factor of 800 and is rough: rsi5/results_p1/restored_fresh2.json shows 32% of candidates kept at 10^6 (median pool 324,149), and the kept share at toy budgets is not known. replicate.py lines 180-186 give the row order (four rows that include fresh3, then C1:heldB, C2:heldB, C2:fresh3). hybrid.py docstring: 'The pool is an executor that never replaces a worker'.
findings.proposed_change: Before committing, run generation 0 once at about 1.7 x 10^6 on four learning-partition tasks that are unsolved at 10^5 (TRAIN or NEAR, not an evaluation set), with the planned worker count, and note peak memory. Add one sentence to 'Mechanism': a restart may use fewer workers, because results do not depend on the worker count (see coverage). Optionally move the two held-out B cumulative rows ahead of the FRESH-3 rows in replicate.py, so a memory crash happens before any FRESH-3 outcome is printed; row order does not change results.

findings.title: replicate.py does not check that it runs on the registered FRESH-3 set
findings.problem: The registration fixes the set by count (300) and digest (333e350613873b88). replicate.py generates the tasks, prints and stores the digest, and continues whatever it is. fresh3.make also returns fewer than COUNT tasks without complaint if the candidates run out, and N in C2 would follow silently. On a different checkout, data file or Python version, a multi-hour run could spend the budget on a set that is not the registered one, and this would be noticed only afterwards by comparing digests by hand.
findings.evidence: replicate.py lines 131-137: fresh_tasks = fresh3.make(statistics=tally); the digest is only stored in out['fresh3'] and printed. The only digest comparison is in the --from-loop branch (line 142), against the earlier report, not against the registration. fresh3.make line 122 stops at count, or when candidates are exhausted. findings.title: The pooled comparison uses C1 on held-out B and C2 on FRESH-3; the text does not say so
findings.problem: Addendum 7 lists as secondary 'the same test on held-out B and pooled'. 'The same test' is trained at 10^5 against generation 0 at C2. The code pools the held-out B control at C1, the smaller cumulative budget (about 0.37 of C2 on that set), with the FRESH-3 control at C2. The pooled line will be the most favourable p in the report, because it adds the 124 tasks the combination was chosen on, against the weaker control. Toy run budgets from tiny.json: C1 3050 against C2 8313 on held-out B. The words 'and pooled' in the 'Secondary' sentence of Addendum 7 are the only specification.

Either write 'pooled: held-out B against C1 and FRESH-3 against C2', or have replicate.py also report the pooled test with C2 on both sets and with 'any budget' on both, and name all three in the text. Decides nothing either way, but the text should fix it.

coverage:
Verdict: I found no bug that would make the result invalid or unfair to one arm; the four findings are a false sentence in the text, a crash risk, a missing guard and an unspecified secondary test. Scripts and outputs are in <scratch>/work/implementation (sound_inputs.py, unit_checks.py, state_dep.py, audit_errors.py, sound_stored.py, degenerate.py, classes.py).

Two things to know about how I ran it:
- The permitted --tiny command itself uses control budgets of 3,050, 4,316 and 8,313 candidates per task, above the 2,000 limit; every check of my own stayed at 2,000 or below, with 2 workers.
- --from-loop was not executed end to end (it would have been a third solver run on FRESH-3). I read it, and the data path it changes (report from JSON into spec_without) is covered by the held-out B check below.

What held:
- **Determinism.** fresh3.py gives digest 333e350613873b88, 300 tasks, 469 examined, 283/8/9 by output type, under the default hash seed and PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 7. The toy protocol twice (second with PYTHONHASHSEED=7) gives identical JSON apart from seconds; 117 s, exit 0.
- **Budgets.** By hand T = 2x338x300 + 2x214x1500 = 844,800; C1 3050, C2 8313 on held-out B, C2 4316 on FRESH-3, as in the report. 338 exposed tasks, 214 learning, 124 held-out, 300 FRESH-3.
- **Which partitions each run covers.** Student runs cover the 8 exposed partitions, teacher runs the 6 learning ones, evaluation rows as registered. 'fresh3' is not in Harness.default after add_partition, and its verifier had 0 queries after four runs that did not name it (fresh2: 400 after 4 runs of 100 tasks, one per task per run). The gate and corpus read learning partitions only (by reading).
- **Same machinery.** Components are 'SCfR' in the loop report and in both arms; representation-search routes occur inside the loop.
- **Final vocabulary.** loop.serialise and expert_ablate.spec_without give identical specs for four libraries: the stored 15-symbol one (constant -2, depth-2 symbols), the toy one (constant 10), and two sets of fresh proposals including list[bool] types. At search level, the trained state at 300 via spec_without equals the loop's accepted student run on held-out B. 488 stored program texts survive parse and print.
- **No dependence on worker history or count.** Generation 0 before and after a trained run is identical in every record field, and runs in fresh workers reproduce the protocol's held-out B rows for both arms.
- **Outcome rule and tests.** outcome_class matches the registered table on a 9-case truth table. Rounding p to 5 decimals never crosses 0.05 for any split up to 424 discordant tasks. sign_test(11,4) = 0.05923 and (9,4) = 0.13342. replicate.Sound and paired on the stored results reproduce 44 against 37, with 11 and 4. paired and clustered were checked by hand; the any-budget union and the by-output-type counts by reading and against the toy report.
